teams.heading: Fiji's breakdown pressure cost Italy in Udine, admits coach Roberto Santamaria
teams.body: Santamaria, Italy's forwards coach with a scrum brief, told Tuesday's press session that the Azzurri conceded extra penalties for holding on and side entry at the ruck. He added that Italy knew going in that the Fijians are strong at generating turnovers and exploiting them. Italy made deep breaks through Fiji's defence, he said, yet every such sequence ended in a penalty they could not turn into a try. One drive stalled a metre out. Italy carry a seven-match losing streak into the Twickenham rematch for 11th place.

lead.why: The Italy-selection thread has no new reporting, so the freshest Fiji-angled item is Italy's own account of how Fiji's breakdown won Udine.

teams.heading: Fin Smith carried 11 times in 55 minutes of England's All Blacks win
teams.body: The Northampton fly-half racked up that tally in Saturday's 37-12 win over New Zealand before cramp forced him off. It made him England's third-highest carrier, behind a Ben Earl he called "greedy" for his 32 carries. Oval Insights figures have Smith carrying more than any other fly-half in a Six Nations side this year. "I would hate to be someone that is asking everyone else to go and be physical and put their body on the line, if I wasn't particularly willing to do it," he told BBC Sport.

lead.why: It is the only new England story, a fly-half explaining the physical edge in Saturday's rematch-winning attack.

teams.heading: Thomas Ramos and Jean-Baptiste Gros expected back for Springboks final at Twickenham
teams.body: Rugbyrama reports that Ramos, finally clear of the thigh injury that kept him out of France's first three November Tests, should start at full-back in Sunday's Nations Championship final at Twickenham. His return eases a back-three reshuffle forced by Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang's ankle injury against Argentina, with Théo Attissogbe moving back to the wing. Kalvin Gourgues is expected to hand the goal-kicking to his Toulouse teammate. Fit-again Gros should reclaim the No. 1 jersey, which is timely after France conceded nine scrum penalties to the Boks in Paris.

lead.why: Fresh, France-centred selection news: two key men expected back for the final, which reshapes the back three and the front row.

teams.heading: Beirne leads Ireland against Australia in Nations Championship fifth-place final
teams.body: Beirne takes the armband for the fifth-place final against Australia at Twickenham. Dan Sheehan, sent off late in the 20-17 win over South Africa, has picked up a two-game suspension. For Australia, Alaalatoa reaches his 100th Test, and Beale's five-year Wallaby exile is set to end. Ireland already have the better of these Wallabies this year. They won 33-31 in July's Southern Series opener, then went three from three in the autumn against Argentina, Fiji and the Springboks.

lead.why: Fresh selection news for the next Test: Beirne has the Ireland captaincy against Australia.

teams.heading: Italy lose Domingo Miotti and Simone Ferrari to injury before Fiji rematch
teams.body: Domingo Miotti went off after 48 minutes of the 16-21 defeat to Fiji in Udine with an injury to the flexor muscles of his left thigh, according to the Italy medical bulletin. Simone Ferrari, named in the matchday squad, withdrew an hour before kick-off with a left upper-limb injury and was replaced by Marco Riccioni. Both were to undergo scans in camp before returning to Montpellier and Treviso respectively to rehabilitate alongside national-team staff. Paolo Garbisi returns at fly-half for Friday's 11th-place final at Twickenham.

lead.why: The medical bulletin confirming two injuries to Italy's squad is the strongest Italy story the reader has not yet seen.

teams.heading: BBC's Burke and English ask if Argentina is Townsend's last selection chance
teams.body: Answering listeners' questions on BBC Radio Scotland's rugby podcast, Andy Burke and Tom English asked whether the seventh-place play-off against Argentina is Townsend's last opportunity to play around with selections before the World Cup, and whether Scotland can move on to the Six Nations with confidence. Fewer pieces are available to move: Matt Fagerson is out with a jaw injury from the 67-5 win over Japan, and Tuesday's squad update made no mention of Nathan McBeth, forced off with an ankle injury in that match.

lead.why: The newest Scotland-focused item not already run. It frames the Argentina play-off around Townsend's selection choices before the World Cup.

teams.heading: Jac Morgan demands Wales finish on a high against Japan at Twickenham
teams.body: Wales's open-side wants the Nations Championship signed off properly, saying it is important to "finish off on a bit of a high" in Saturday's ninth-place final at Twickenham. Morgan started all three Cardiff Tests and is one of 11 players to do so, with Tandy set to freshen his side for a rematch of this month's nervy 28-21 win over the Brave Blossoms. The flanker said the players who have missed out have been "challenging and competitive" in preparing the starters.

lead.why: It is the only new story about the senior side's coming Test: the open-side's demand alongside Tandy's planned freshen-up for Japan.

teams.heading: Contepomi adds six to Pumas squad, Matías Moroni one cap from 100
teams.body: Felipe Contepomi has reinforced for Sunday's seventh-place final against Scotland after losing Mayco Vivas to his red card in Paris, Bautista Delguy to a knee injury, Mateo Carreras to a shoulder problem and Pablo Matera for personal reasons. Ignacio Ruiz, Julián Montoya's regular understudy, returns with flanker Santiago Grondona. Loosehead Rodrigo Martínez, wing Santiago Pernas and uncapped fly-half Juan Segundo Martín Montilla also come in. If Moroni plays, the centre will become the second Pumas back to reach 100 caps after Nicolás Sánchez. He has played at three World Cups.

lead.why: Contepomi's six additions to the squad for the Scotland game, including Moroni on 99 caps, are the freshest Argentina selection news not yet led.

teams.heading: Les Kiss's Wallabies get Ireland rematch after July's 31-33 loss
teams.body: Friday's fifth-place final at Twickenham is the second meeting of the campaign, Ireland having won the Southern Series opener on 4 July. The Wallabies followed it by losing 26-42 to France before beating Italy 57-10. Their autumn form has been patchier than Ireland's: Les Kiss's side lost to England and Scotland before winning in Cardiff, while Andy Farrell's men went three from three against Argentina, Fiji and world champions South Africa.

lead.why: The pack's only new men's 15s Australia item, a rematch of July's two-point defeat; Sheehan's ban has already run and the sevens item is women's rugby.

teams.heading: Japan's Twickenham opponents Wales lose fly-half Dan Edwards to ankle injury
teams.body: Japan will not see Edwards in Saturday's ninth-place final. The outside-half, who missed Wales' narrow defeat to Australia last weekend with an ankle injury, is in a boot and could face a spell on the sidelines. Sam Costelow, Joe Hawkins and Jarrod Evans are the contenders to start at No. 10 for the side that beat Japan 28-21 in round four. Forwards coach Danny Wilson also said lock Adam Beard, absent against Australia with a shoulder injury, is back in full training.

lead.why: The only NEW item is a TV-listings guide with no Japan squad, selection, injury or coach news, so the opponent's fly-half injury before Saturday's final is the strongest unreported story.

teams.heading: Beauden Barrett and Wallace Sititi reportedly heading to Europe after World Cup
teams.body: The Times reports that the 35-year-old Blues back, who brought up his 150th Test in last weekend's 37-12 defeat at Twickenham, has signed a two-year deal with Bristol Bears worth around £2 million, with an official announcement expected once the Nations Championship is done. Midi Olympique has Sititi, the Chiefs No. 8 whose New Zealand Rugby contract runs to the end of 2027, lined up for a two-year move to Stade Français. Both would follow Luke Jacobson, already reported to be bound for Bayonne.

lead.why: A fresh transfer report on two senior All Blacks, Beauden Barrett and Wallace Sititi, is the newest New Zealand event in the pack and has not run before.

teams.heading: Pieter-Steph du Toit ruled out of France final, Rassie delays replacement call
teams.body: The blindside flanker, named to start Sunday's Nations Championship final against France, has withdrawn with a niggle and returns to South Africa alongside Damian Willemse, who took a knock against Ireland. SA Rugby said Erasmus will confirm changes to the match-23 later in the week once he decides whether to call a replacement to London. Bench pick Emmanuel Tshituka, in line for a Test debut, could fill the gap, while Marco van Staden awaits the verdict of a disciplinary hearing after his red card for a shoulder charge.

lead.why: Du Toit's withdrawal is a material new development: a named starter is out of Sunday's final and the replacement is still undecided.
